ai-at-work.title: What ClickUp’s mass layoff tells us about the future of work
ai-at-work.excerpt: The nine-year-old startup is replacing hundreds of employees with thousands of AI agents.
ai-at-work.dwp_take: ClickUp just cut hundreds of employees and replaced them with AI agents to handle their internal workflows. This matters because it's a real-world test case of what happens when a productivity software company actually eats its own dog food at scale, and right now the results look messy. Here's the thing: if ClickUp can't figure out how to integrate AI without mass layoffs, that tells you something important about the gap between AI hype and actual workplace reality, and it's worth watching before your CEO gets similar ideas.

ai-at-work.title: Dell and Nvidia target the data chaos standing between AI pilots and real results
ai-at-work.excerpt: As organizations push to convert AI ambition into defensible business results, many are discovering that infrastructure alone is not enough. Instead, the real challenge lies in reconciling decades of
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Dell and Nvidia are basically saying that most companies have a data mess so chaotic that their fancy AI dreams will crash and burn without fixing it first. This matters because digital workplace leaders are about to get asked why their organization's AI pilot failed, and the honest answer is probably "our data looked like a yard sale." The irony is that organizations spent years ignoring data governance, and now they're shocked that AI won't magically make spaghetti organized.

ai-at-work.title: As token costs shoot up, Dell doubles down on desktop AI
ai-at-work.excerpt: As enterprises confront spiraling cloud inference bills, on-prem AI computing is emerging as the decisive lever for making agentic AI economically viable at scale. Dell Technologies Inc.’s announcemen
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Dell is betting that running AI locally on desktops will be cheaper than paying cloud providers for every AI query your employees make. This matters because digital workplace leaders are already drowning in new software costs, and the math on AI infrastructure is genuinely broken right now. Honestly, if local AI actually delivers on the cost promise, it might be the first time a vendor solved a real problem instead of creating three new ones.

tools-tech.title: Q&A: How video helps build robot brains for physical AI
tools-tech.excerpt: Robots could well be the next trillion-dollar tech opportunity, in no small part thanks to AI. Not surprisingly, that’s led to race by a variety of robotics companies to build industrial and humanoid
tools-tech.dwp_take: A bunch of robotics companies are training AI robot brains by feeding them massive amounts of YouTube video data so the robots can actually understand the physical world around them. This matters to digital workplace leaders because if robots start showing up in your offices and warehouses (and they will), those robots are only as smart as the training data they consumed, which means your workplace environments need to be designed with that reality in mind. Here's the thing though: robots trained on random YouTube clips is basically like hiring employees who learned everything they know from TikTok, so manage your expectations accordingly.

digital-culture.title: How AI keeps both job seekers and employers from filling roles
digital-culture.excerpt: Jobseekers and recruiters are at a technological standoff. Candidates upload (and retype) their resumes into an applicant tracking system (ATS) with no sense of whether or not their applications are g
digital-culture.dwp_take: AI-powered applicant tracking systems are so good at filtering candidates that perfectly qualified people never get seen, while recruiters still drown in applications. This matters because your internal hiring process probably has the same problem: you're using technology that's supposed to solve recruitment friction but actually just hides candidates behind another wall. The irony is that we've built systems so efficient at rejecting people that we've made it harder than ever to actually find talent.

digital-culture.title: The hidden cost of workplace transformation: How change initiatives crush top employees
digital-culture.excerpt: Nearly half of employees report experiencing "transformation fatigue," according to a recent study
digital-culture.dwp_take: Half your workforce is burnt out from constant change initiatives, and nobody's really talking about the cost of losing your best people in the process. Digital workplace professionals need to understand that transformation fatigue is real and it directly impacts adoption rates, productivity, and retention of the talent you actually need. Here's the truth: announcing another shiny new tool or process without letting people catch their breath is a great way to watch your A-players quietly update their LinkedIn profiles.

digital-culture.title: Technology x humanity: A conversation with Dayforce’s Amy Capellanti-Wolf
digital-culture.excerpt: The HR leader shares her take on the rise of AI, hybrid work and retaining talent.
digital-culture.dwp_take: Dayforce's Amy Capellanti-Wolf is making the rounds talking about AI, hybrid work, and keeping people from bolting to competitors. This matters because HR leaders are the ones actually living with the technology decisions IT makes, so when they speak up about what's working and what's not, it's worth listening to instead of ignoring them. The "technology x humanity" angle is refreshing because it acknowledges that throwing AI at your retention problem won't work if your hybrid policy still requires butts in seats on Tuesdays.

digital-culture.title: Workforce data, smarter AI integration among greatest workplace priorities in the new year
digital-culture.excerpt: The importance of workforce data is just one of the prognostications people managers are making looking to the year ahead.
digital-culture.dwp_take: Organizations are finally treating workforce data as a strategic asset instead of something IT shoves into a spreadsheet and forgets about. This matters because digital workplace professionals need to understand that data governance and AI integration aren't technical problems anymore, they're business problems that will either make or break employee experience initiatives. Here's the thing though: most companies will talk a big game about "smarter AI integration" while their actual data is still a mess, and that gap between intention and reality is where most projects go to die.

digital-culture.title: Hermes Agentic AI Overtakes OpenClaw, 10 Shifts Leaders Need To Know
digital-culture.excerpt: Hermes Agent overtakes OpenClaw as agentic systems accelerate. Learn the 10 key agentic shifts reshaping enterprise strategy, speed, and execution today.
digital-culture.dwp_take: Hermes Agentic AI has apparently surpassed OpenClaw in some capability metric, and Forbes is suggesting this signals major shifts in how enterprises should think about autonomous AI agents. This matters because agentic AI will eventually touch your workplace tech stack, your support processes, and how knowledge workers actually get things done. Here's the thing though: "10 key shifts" listicles rarely survive contact with your actual infrastructure, legacy systems, and the reality that your org moves at human speed no matter what the AI can do.

digital-culture.title: How To Use AI Agents To Streamline Email Sorting And Boost Productivity
digital-culture.excerpt: Learn how to use an AI agent to sort emails, automate your inbox, and save time with simple tools and step-by-step instructions.
digital-culture.dwp_take: Forbes is pushing AI agents as the answer to email overload, suggesting they can automatically sort and organize your inbox with minimal setup. This matters because email chaos is still eating up real productivity time in most organizations, and if AI can actually reduce that friction without creating new problems, it's worth evaluating. The reality though is that most people's email problems stem from terrible folder discipline and unclear communication norms, not missing technology, so don't expect an AI agent to fix what's fundamentally a people and process issue.

digital-culture.title: Digital sovereignty, the musical: One engineer’s bizarre crusade against hyperscalers
digital-culture.excerpt: A French engineer has declared war on AWS, Google and Microsoft using AI-generated sea shanties, satirical poetry, and a multilingual protest campaign
digital-culture.dwp_take: A French engineer has taken his frustration with big cloud providers and turned it into an absurdist art project featuring AI sea shanties and multilingual protest poetry instead of, you know, filing actual complaints or building alternatives. Digital workplace professionals should care because this highlights real sovereignty concerns that deserve serious attention, even if the delivery mechanism is completely unhinged. Look, I'm all for creative protest, but if you've got legitimate gripes about vendor lock-in and data residency, maybe skip the musical number and just write a technical white paper like a normal person.
